title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook combines Redwood Inference's standard enterprise onboarding sequence, escalation flow, integration checklist, common known issues and workarounds, and Health Check / QBR guidance into a single operational reference for CSMs, SEs, and Support Engineers. Use this document to drive consistent customer ramp, reduce time-to-first-success, and ensure reliable escalation behavior for production incidents and quality regressions.

1) Purpose and scope
- Scope: enterprise customers onboarding to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers (Tier 1-3), Product/Engineering leads, and Customer Contacts.

2) High-level onboarding stages
- Sales handoff: contractual details, SSO/KMS requirements, and point-of-contact alignment.
- Kickoff (Week 0): project plan, goals, success metrics, legal/compliance checklist.
- Integration (Week 1-4): API keys, routing, network connectivity (VPC), model selection, and latency benchmarking.
- Optimization (Week 4-8): batching, caching, quantization recommendations, cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Stabilize & QBR cadence (Month 2+): weekly then monthly QBRs, health checks, and SLA reviews.

3) Onboarding checklist (CSM / SE responsibilities)
- Pre-kickoff: Confirm account admin, billing contact, and data residency requirements.
- Kickoff agenda: Introductions, objectives, timeline, risk assessment, security posture.
- Tech tasks:
  - Create API keys and scoped roles.
  - Verify network egress/IP allowlist for Hosted endpoints or setup Private control plane tunnel.
  - Provide model catalog recommendation (low-latency vs high-quality).
  - Run initial perf test: 100 requests at target input lengths, record p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec.
- Acceptance criteria: Production traffic with <5% error rate for 72 hours and p95 latency within agreed SLO.

4) Integration guide (abridged)
- Supported flows: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming.
- API basics: use per-route keys for rate limiting; prefer streaming for long-form responses.
- VPC/Private deployment notes: confirm customer firewall settings, DNS routing, and KMS key access.
- Example CLI test:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.company/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Hello"}'
- Integration checklist table:
  | Item | Owner | Success criteria |
  |------|-------|------------------|
  | API key scoped | SE | Test call succeeds and returns 200 |
  | Network | Customer/SE | Hosted: test IP allowlist; Private: VPN validated |
  | Model choice | SE/Product | Baseline perf recorded |
  | Logging | Customer/CSM | Audit logs enabled and forwarded if required |

5) Escalation matrix and process
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev 1 (Critical): Production outage or >50% customers affected, data loss risk, or SLA breach imminent.
  - Sev 2 (High): Degraded performance (p95 latency >2x SLO) for critical routes or >10% errors.
  - Sev 3 (Medium): Functional issue with workaround; partial feature regression.
  - Sev 4 (Low): Minor UI/UX issues, documentation requests, or feature requests.
- Escalation steps (numbered):
  1. Triage at Tier 1: gather logs, request IDs, timestamps, and request customer impact.
  2. If unresolved within 30 minutes (Sev1) or 2 hours (Sev2), escalate to Tier 2 (Support Engineer).
  3. Tier 2 performs live debugging, engages serving-runtime on-call (Tier 3) if kernel/resource issues suspected.
  4. For Sev1, notify SRE and product lead; start incident bridge within 15 minutes.
  5. Communicate updates to customer every 30 minutes (Sev1) or hourly (Sev2) until resolution.
- Ownership and contacts:
  - Tier 1: Support Team (support@redwoodinference.company)
  - Tier 2: Support Engineers (rotating pager)
  - Tier 3 / Serving Runtime: eng-serving-runtime on-call (pager)
  - Customer Success escalation: CSM on-call listed in Salesforce record

6) Runbook excerpts (common scenarios)
- High error-rate on generation route:
  1. Collect recent request IDs and sample payloads.
  2. Check model variant fallbacks and capacity routing logs.
  3. Verify KV cache eviction and memory pressure on serving hosts.
  4. If capacity shortage, invoke automatic fallback to compatible model variant; notify customer of temporary downgrade.
- Elevated p95 latency:
  1. Confirm batching settings and per-route batch windows.
  2. Review GPU utilization and slow RPCs in observability dashboard.
  3. If hardware saturation, open capacity request with eng-infra and enable burst pools for the customer.

7) Known issues and workarounds (snapshot)
- Issue: Intermittent streaming cutoffs for long outputs (>8k tokens).
  - Symptom: client receives incomplete stream and connection closes.
  - Workaround: enable chunked streaming with keepalive pings; set streaming buffer to 64KB.
- Issue: Private deployment KMS key rotation causes auth failures.
  - Symptom: API calls return 401 after rotation window.
  - Workaround: coordinate rotation window, provide temporary key, and run post-rotation smoke tests.
- Known issues table:
  | ID | Symptom | Workaround | Owner | ETA fix |
  |----|--------|-----------|-------|---------|
  | CS-101 | Streaming cutoffs | Chunked streaming + keepalive | eng-serving-runtime | 2026-11-01 |
  | CS-117 | KMS rotation fail | Coordination + temp key | eng-private-deployments | 2026-10-15 |

8) Health checks and QBR materials
- Standard health check metrics (weekly):
  - API error rate (5xx) — target <0.5%
  - p50/p95/p99 latency per route — target p95 within SLA
  - Cost per 1k tokens and tokens/sec throughput to detect regressions
  - Model quality regressions (based on eval prompt-set): false positive/negative rates
- QBR agenda template (monthly or quarterly depending on customer tier):
  1. Business review: adoption metrics and ROI examples.
  2. Operational review: uptime, SLOs, incident summary since last QBR.
  3. Performance review: latency and cost trends, optimization opportunities.
  4. Roadmap alignment: product/features impacting customer use-cases.
  5. Action items and owners.
- Deliverables: health dashboard snapshot, incident RCA summaries, and optimization playbook with actionable recommendations.

9) SLAs, SLOs and reporting
- Default Hosted SLOs:
  - Availability: 99.9% monthly for production endpoints
  - Latency: p95 generation latency target depends on model class; default p95 target = 500ms for short-form models, 2s for long-form heavy models (documented per-model).
- Reporting cadence: weekly health emails, monthly QBR slides, and immediate incident postmortems for Sev1 events.

10) Handoff and graduation criteria
- Graduation to self-serve support occurs when:
  - 30 days of stable production with <=1 Sev2 incident and error rate <1%.
  - CSM and customer sign-off on knowledge transfer and runbook access.

11) Templates and attachments (links)
- Kickoff slide deck template: link: /templates/enterprise-kickoff-deck
- Perf test script (curl and python examples): link: /tools/perf-test-scripts
- QBR slide template: link: /templates/qbr-template

12) Ownership and escalation SLAs for internal teams
- Support Tier 1 acknowledges Sev1 within 5 minutes during business hours; outside hours follow pager rota.
- Serving-runtime on-call joins Sev1 bridge within 15 minutes.
- Eng-infra to respond to confirmed capacity incidents within 60 minutes.

13) FAQ and tips
- Tip: For latency-sensitive routes, prefer smaller model variants + aggressive KV caching.
- FAQ: How to test failover? Use staged traffic with canary routing and verify fallback logs.
